messages:
sophia: Heads up — Pegasus (dedicated) fleet: after the kernel rollout at 03:15 we saw tail latency regressions for long-context requests. p50 42ms -> 48ms, p95 310ms -> 420ms, p99 520ms -> 780ms. Throughput down ~30% for seq_len >= 1024. Can eng-runtime triage? /cc @andrew @kai

andrew: looking. do we have a repro prompt + profile traces?

sophia: repro attached to the canary job (logs + perf profile). KV cache hit rate stable (~78%) so KV likely not the culprit. Noticed autokernel selected int8-fused-attn on A100s; previous kernel was fp16-unfused. Also batching window spiked because queue_policy defaulted to larger window after change.

kai: int8-fused-attn can be faster for short sequences but worse for long sequences — that matches this. can you paste kernel selection snippet from the canary logs?

sophia: sure, snippet:
```
kernel_select: model=pegasus-v2, seq=1024 -> kernel=int8-fused-attn, est_tokens_per_ms=0.8
prev_kernel: fp16-unfused-attn, est_tokens_per_ms=1.1
batcher: continuous_batcher window_ms=80 -> 160 (observed)
```

marta: ops view: customer (Pegasus Inc) current dedicated config: token_budget_per_worker=3000, queue_ceiling=1800. They asked for lower tail latencies but also want cost control. My initial suggestion: token_budget_per_worker=2500, queue_ceiling=1200, continuous_batcher window_ms=100, and enable kv_cache_prefetch=true.

andrew: let's test a minimal set: (1) reduce batch window, (2) enable kernel override to force fp16-unfused for seq >= 768, (3) keep token_budget conservative. Canary at 5% traffic. Also add telemetry tag so we can trace kernel decisions in dashboard.

chris: +1. Add rule-based fallback: if p95 > 500ms for 10m then fallback kernel to fp16 automatically. Also log kernel switch events.

ops-bot: deploy request queued: /deploy canary config peg-pegasus-20260312-batch-tweak (canary=5%)

sophia: running canary now with: 
```json
{
  "queue_policy": "token_budget",
  "token_budget_per_worker": 2500,
  "queue_ceiling": 1200,
  "continuous_batcher_window_ms": 100,
  "kernel_override": "fp16-unfused if seq>=768",
  "kv_cache_prefetch": true
}
```
I'll post results in ~20m.

[20m later]

sophia: canary results: 5% traffic, kernel override -> p50=44ms, p95=290ms, p99=420ms. Throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline; long-seq throughput much closer to expected. KV hit rate unchanged. No regressions in short-seq tail.

kai: solid. kernel override fixed the worst part. sounds safe to propose as customer config.

marta: proposed rollout plan to customer: token_budget_per_worker=2500, queue_ceiling=1200, continuous_batcher_window_ms=100, kernel_override rule 'seq>=768 -> fp16-unfused', fallback rule: if p95>500ms rollback kernel. Canary 5% -> 25% after 1h if stable -> 100% after 4h. Cost impact estimate: +~4% GPU cycles.

andrew: i'll draft the dedicated-config change note and runbook: steps to apply, rollback, and telemetry to verify (kernel_tag, p95, kv_hit). Also add test in perf harness to validate seq=1024 workload.

sophia: pinging @pegasus-cs (customer success) in customer thread to get signoff. once customer ok, we schedule canary rollout.

chris: tiny follow-up: can we add an automated kernel-selection test to CI that runs short/long seq microbenchmarks and flags regressions? would have caught this earlier.

andrew: good call. adding to eng-runtime backlog.

sophia: thanks everyone — marking thread resolved for now, will re-open if customer reports anything after rollout. :thumbsup:
